value: Study analyzed >6,500 metagenomes from 36 datasets across 6 continents and 25 countries
Generated 1,023 high-quality P. copri genomes: 17 isolates, 1,006 metagenome-assembled genomes
P. copri comprises four genetically distinct clades (A, B, C, D) with >10% inter-clade genetic divergence
All four clades significantly more prevalent in non-Westernized vs Westernized populations (p<1.1e-12)
Analyzed 10 disease cohorts: colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, inflammatory bowel disease
Found no strong evidence linking specific P. copri clades to disease etiology
Reconstructed 98 additional genomes from non-Westernized populations in Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Madagascar
Ancient metagenome analysis: P. copri present in 5,300-year-old Iceman and pre-Columbian Mexican coprolites
Clade divergence estimated 6.5 million years ago (clade B split) to 2.5-3.5 million years ago (clades A, D, C)
Substantial functional diversity in carbohydrate metabolism between clades
Clade B enriched in pectin-degrading families PL9 and PL10
Clade D enriched in GH9 cellulase family
Multi-generational dietary modifications hypothesized as driver of reduced prevalence in Westernized populations
19.2% (5/26) intra-family strain sharing suggesting possible horizontal/vertical transmission
